title: Balancing a pole
summary: An unstable system, a PID loop that half works, an LQR that does the job, and what a weak motor does to it all.

steps.title: It falls
steps.text: A pole balanced upright on a cart is unstable: the smallest tilt grows. Open the Analyze ▸ Modes tab for the cart without control: one mode is a Topple (unstable), with a positive eigenvalue of about 4.0 per second, so a tilt grows e-fold every quarter second. Run it to see.

check.success: The other modes: the cart drifting freely (eigenvalue 0), its speed dying away under friction (−0.09 per second), and the topple's mirror image at −4.0 per second: a tilt already swinging toward upright at just the right rate comes to rest there.

steps.title: PID on the angle
steps.text: Push the cart under the pole when it leans: F = Kp θ + Ki ∫θ + Kd θ'. Run the PID controller. The pole stays up (max |θ| about 5°, the starting tilt), but watch the cart in the Angle and position tab: nothing tells it where to be, so it wanders off.

check.success: Balanced, but the cart drifted almost 2 m. The Analyze ▸ Modes tab shows a Cart drift (neutral) mode.

steps.title: LQR: balance and return
steps.text: A linear-quadratic regulator uses the whole state, s = [x ẋ θ θ'], and picks the gains K that minimize ∫ (sᵀ Q s + r F²) dt. Run it: the pole recovers and the cart comes back to the middle. The Gains and poles tab shows K and every closed-loop pole in the left half-plane.

check.success: Both the pole and the cart are under control.

steps.title: Cheaper control
steps.text: The weight r prices the force. Raise it from 0.1 to 10 and run: the controller pushes more gently (compare Max |F| in the Summary, about 6.8 N before) and takes longer to settle.

check.hint: Set the LQR weight on force (r) to 10 and run.
check.success: Less force, slower recovery: the trade-off LQR lets you tune with one number.

steps.title: Motor limits
steps.text: Real motors have a force limit. With a 10° start and only 2 N, the motor saturates: the cart races along under the pole, overshoots, and reaches the end of the track as the pole falls back the other way. Find a force limit that is just enough: raise Fmax until the pole settles, using as little as you can (5 N or less).

check.success: 2.81 N is the least that works (2.8 N is just too little; 3 N settles in about 2.5 s, 4 N in 1.25 s): the controller still works while saturated, as long as it can recover before the pole tips too far.
